instructions:
# Annotate all 120 pages: region selection and four line types

Please inspect every page in this archive using BOTH the full-resolution image
and its aligned OCR. Return a ZIP of completed semantic annotations. The goal is
training a classifier that transfers across these ten early printed Latin books.
There are 100 training pages and 20 evaluation pages; annotate both sets but keep
their existing split unchanged. Do not stop after a few examples.

## Input files

- `manifest.json` and `pages.csv`: exact 120-page inventory, image paths and hashes,
  dimensions, book/scan identities, counts, and the fixed training/evaluation split.
- `images/<book>/<scan>.jpg`: all original images, unchanged at full resolution.
- `previews/<book>/<scan>.jpg`: smaller navigation previews; orange numbered region
  boxes and blue line boxes. R01 etc. map to `display_id` in the page JSON. Use the
  ORIGINAL image for reading and fine detail; previews are not coordinate space.
- `pages/<book>/<scan>.json`: every region with its stable ID, box and polygon,
  containing its own lines with IDs, boxes, polygons, baselines, OCR and confidence.
  Native floating-point line geometry is also retained. OCR belongs to these exact
  PERO lines; never pair text and geometry from different line sets or list positions.
- `ocr/<book>/<scan>.txt`: the same OCR grouped by region, with each line's ID.
- `pagexml/<book>/<scan>.xml`: portable PAGE XML with regions, lines and OCR.
- `annotation_templates/<book>/<scan>.json`: an output template for EVERY page,
  EVERY region and EVERY line, initially pending. Copy to `annotations/` and fill it.
- `annotation.schema.json`: output structure; `coverage_template.json`: page checklist.
- `review_flags.json`: possible duplicate boxes and regions with no detected lines.
- `provenance/`: sampling/split policy and model/source hashes; `checksums.sha256`:
  checksums of all other archive members.

Coordinates in JSON and PAGE XML use original image pixels: x right, y down,
`bbox = [left, top, right, bottom]`. Do not use resized-preview coordinates.
IDs are unique within a page; always identify an object by page key plus its ID.

## 1. Select the pertinent regions

Determine which physical regions contain the primary legal material whose logical
parts are being annotated: the source legal text, its attribution, introducing
summary, and associated chapter/title headings and initials. Distinguish these from
surrounding gloss/commentary, references, running headers, folios and artifacts.
The small primary passage can be surrounded by much larger commentary blocks.

Set each region's `selection` to `pertinent`, `not_pertinent`, `mixed`, or `uncertain`.
Use `mixed` if a supplied box contains both pertinent and excluded material; select
its lines individually. For excluded regions give a brief reason such as gloss,
running header or false detection. A pertinent region can contain several line types;
do not force one semantic class onto the whole region.

The semantic roles are not decided solely by box position, type size, italics or red
ink. Read the Latin and the surrounding passage. Different printers use different
typographic conventions: an attribution can be red or black, small or text-size.

## 2. Label the lines within the selected regions

For every pertinent line set `in_scope: true` and `semantic_label` to ONE of:

- `summarium`: editorial abstract/summary of the legal passage, often introducing
  it; distinguish it from surrounding commentary by both content and context.
- `inscriptio`: attribution/source or issuing authority for the passage, including
  pope/emperor/author and relevant addressee or abbreviated attribution such as Idem.
- `text`: the primary legal passage itself.
- `other`: associated primary-text headings (CAP., TITULUS, etc.), decorative initials
  and other pertinent material that does not fit the three roles above.

Excluded gloss is NOT `other`: use `in_scope: false`, `semantic_label: null` and a
reason. Also account for every line in a non-pertinent region this way. Keep the
exact original region and line IDs so the result can be joined to the geometry/OCR.

For a genuinely mixed-role line, mark `review_status: needs_review`; use optional
`semantic_spans` with zero-based start/end character offsets into the supplied OCR
(end exclusive), one of the four labels, and the exact corresponding substring.
Do not invent a fifth line type or silently force a mixed line into a wrong label.
A null line label is allowed only for excluded or explicitly unresolved lines.
If a mixed line has a clear whole-line label, record it as well as the exception.
For OCR too damaged to align spans reliably, describe the issue in `note` instead.
Use the image when the OCR is wrong; optional `corrected_text` must be separate from
the original OCR, which remains unchanged in `pages/`.

## Geometry and coverage

This is a semantic annotation pass. Keep supplied geometry and IDs unchanged.
Distinct touching regions must remain distinct. If a box/line is merged, missing,
duplicated or otherwise misleading, record the problem in `geometry_issues` with
affected IDs and a description. Do not silently remove it or create invented text.
When the image confirms duplicate region detections, set `duplicate_of` to the
canonical region ID and exclude the redundant region and its lines; retain all IDs.
Overlap flags are suggestions, not proof of duplication. Empty detected regions may
be initials, illustrations or missed text; inspect them rather than assuming blank.

Inspect all 120 images, including difficult pages and all 13 blank OCR lines.
Do not infer hundreds of labels from typography alone, fabricate a human review,
or claim coverage without examining the evidence. The input has 2,392 region
instances and 32,018 lines. There are no supplied semantic classifier predictions.

## Return

Return a ZIP with `annotations/<book>/<scan>.json` for all 120 pages, following the
templates and schema; `coverage.json` (filled from the checklist); and `REPORT.md`
listing counts and unresolved cases. Images need not be returned. Preserve `key`,
`partition`, `image_sha256`, every region ID and every line ID exactly. Set each
reviewed object's `review_status` to `reviewed` or `needs_review`. Set a page to
`complete` only when all its objects are accounted for with no pending or unresolved
decisions; otherwise use `partial`. State page/region/line coverage explicitly.

Label these as `annotation_source: webgpt`, `human_gold: false`: they are LLM
annotations for subsequent review, not independently validated human gold. If you
cannot finish all 120, return the completed work plus a precise unfinished list;
do not claim full completion or substitute a handful of examples.
